1: # CLAUDE.md — Dungeon Haul
2: 
3: Instructions for AI agents (Claude Code and similar) working in this repository.
4: 
5: ## What this project is
6: 
7: **Dungeon Haul** is a remake of a TOJam 8 local multiplayer sidescroller: four haulers loot a dungeon, navigate traps, sabotage each other, and split the haul via **Share Modifiers**. This remake makes **online multiplayer first-class** (authoritative server, drop-in/reconnect, AI fill for empty seats).

44: | Platforms | Desktop evergreen browsers only (Chrome / Firefox / Safari / Edge) |
45: | Matchmaking | Private room codes only for MVP |
46: | Couch co-op | Online seats first; local multi-gamepad is stretch |
47: | Level progression | Random unplayed pair at each fork (not full path graph for MVP) |
48: | Resolution | **960×540** logical, integer scale, letterbox |
49: | Hosting | Fly.io (or Railway) sticky processes for game rooms |
50: | Identity | No accounts; ephemeral names + high-score initials |
51: | Run length | `levelsAfterHoard` configurable; default **2** for playtests, **7** full |
52: | Characters | Soft-unique (prefer distinct; allow clash) |
53: | Pause | No global pause in MVP (local menu only) |

57: - Exactly **4** hauler seats in game state; AI fills inactive/disconnected seats
58: - Client never computes official takes — only displays server `ScoreReport`
59: - Share formula: `take = totalTreasure × (shares_i / sum shares)` with **min 1 share**

112: 
113: ### 5.1 Coordinate space
114: 
115: - World units: pixels; **blockSizePx = 32** (assumption until art locks).

119: ### 5.2 Hauler kinematics (conceptual)
120: 
121: ```text
122: HaulerBody {
123:   x, y, vx, vy
124:   halfW, halfH          // duck shortens halfH
125:   grounded: bool
126:   facing: 1 | -1
127:   jumpBufferedUntilTick?
128:   coyoteUntilTick?      // optional feel polish; document if used
129: }
130: ```

132: **MVP movement set**
133: 
134: | Action | Behavior |
135: |---|---|
136: | Run | Accelerate toward `axes.x * maxSpeed * speedMultiplier` |
137: | Jump | On grounded + jump edge → set `vy` to jump velocity × `jumpMultiplier` |
138: | Air steer | Reduced accel vs ground |
139: | Duck | `axes.y == +1` (down); enables pickup; shrinks hitbox |
140: | Gravity | Constant acceleration while airborne |
141: | Surfaces | Ice: low friction; Sand: high friction / lower max speed; Brick: default |

146: 
147: - Static: solid cells from `LevelDefinition.cells` (brick, ice, sand, closed gates, etc.).

231: 
232: ### 7.1 Spawn
233: 
234: - On level load: for each `treasureSlots[]`, roll via C-07 `rollTreasureDef(rng, table, ctx)`.  
235: - World mix target: **65% Common, 20% Rare, 5% Unique, 10% Set** (design).

239: ### 7.2 Ownership
240: 
241: | Action | Rules |
242: |---|---|
243: | Pickup | Duck near free instance; grant only if not lockout and free; server sole grantor |
244: | Drop | Chord action+down: detach top stack item near feet |
245: | Throw | Chord action+up: detach top with velocity (facing); becomes projectile then free |
246: | Steal | Only via free world instances (after spill/drop/throw), never client claim |
247: | Pit | May **destroy** instance; increment `treasureLostCount` for last owner if tracked |

249: ### 7.3 Spill (Sonic-style)
250: 
251: On **stun** (trap, severe hit):
252: 
253: 1. All (or policy subset) carried items detach with outward velocities.  
254: 2. Owner gets `pickupLockoutUntilTick` so others can steal.  
255: 3. Emit `spill` + `stun` events.  
256: 4. Stats: `stunnedOrHurtCount`, `treasureLostCount` as items leave ownership.

258: ### 7.4 Conservation invariant
259: 
260: - Every `instanceId` is either: carried by one seat, free in world, or destroyed (logged).  
261: - Never two owners. Tests assert this under racey multi-seat pickup tapes.

10: ## 1. Purpose
11: 
12: Fill inactive hauler seats so Game State always has **exactly 4 active haulers**. AI produces the same `InputCommand` shape as humans and is applied by the authoritative simulation (C-06) — it never mutates world state directly.
13: 
14: Goals:
15: 
16: 1. Keep pace with humans (average-position flocking).
17: 2. Collect nearby treasure without hogging beyond the greediest human.
18: 3. Press switches/buttons so co-op gates don’t soft-lock solo runs.
19: 4. Soft-handoff on disconnect/idle takeover and human drop-in.
20: 
21: Non-goals (MVP):
22: 
23: - Pathfinding perfection, jumps over complex traps, or ML.
24: - Difficulty scaling or per-character personality.
25: - Griefy sabotage (trip/throw at humans) unless later design adds it.

29: ## 2. Responsibilities & non-responsibilities

31: ### Responsibilities
32: 
33: | Area | Detail |
34: |---|---|
35: | Per-tick decisions | For each seat with `control == AI`, emit one `InputCommand` |
36: | Position bias | Move toward average **human** position within a tolerance band |
37: | Treasure greed | Pickup nearby free treasure; upgrade load (drop lesser → pick greater) |
38: | Load cap | Never carry more items than the **max human carry count** this tick |
39: | Switches | Prefer pressing nearby unpressed switches/buttons when in range |
40: | Phase gating | **No AI on Instructions** — server does not request AI cmds there |
41: | Fill policy | AI pilots empty, disconnected (grace), and idle-timeout seats |
42: | Fork policy | Mild argue policy so forks resolve without humans (MVP) |
43: 
44: ### Non-responsibilities
45: 
46: - Physics, collision, pickup grant, chord interpretation (C-06).
47: - Idle timeout detection ownership (C-06 / room) — AI only reacts once `control` flips.
48: - Client-side prediction of AI haulers (remote interpolation is enough).
49: - High-score eligibility (AI never submits).
50: - Trap “AI” for golems/phantom hands (those are sim entities).

156: ## 6. Control lifecycle (fill / takeover)
157: 
158: Owned primarily by **room + sim**; AI controller only produces cmds when `control == AI`.
159: 
160: | Event | Seat `control` | AI role |
161: |---|---|---|
162: | Session start / lobby empty seats | `ai` (or `empty` until Hoard) | Stand idle or inactive until Game State |
163: | **Instructions** | No AI seats active | **Do not call** AI for this phase; humans only |
164: | Level / Hoard / Fork / End (non-entry) | Empty human → `ai` | Produce cmds |
165: | Human idle **20s** no packets | → `ai` | Soft takeover: keep pos/inventory |
166: | Human idle **5s** + camera-edge pressure | → `ai` | Same |
167: | Human disconnect (grace e.g. 30s) | → `ai` (seat held) | Pilot until reconnect |
168: | Human reconnect / any human input on seat | → `human` | Stop producing cmds that tick |
169: | Soft-takeover on join into AI seat | → `human` | Preserve world state |

181: ## 7. Behavior stack (priority)
182: 
183: Each AI seat evaluates a **priority cascade** once per tick. Highest matching intent wins; lower intents fill residual axes/buttons only if free.
184: 
185: ```text
186: 0. Stunned / forced anim     → zero movement; no jump/action
187: 1. Switch duty               → move to nearest actionable switch; stand/press
188: 2. Treasure upgrade          → drop/throw lesser if better free treasure in range
189: 3. Treasure pickup           → if under load cap and treasure in pickup range
190: 4. Position flock            → move toward average human position (tolerance band)
191: 5. Exit bias (optional)      → if all humans past midpoint toward exit, bias that way
192: 6. Idle                      → axes 0; small hop only if stuck timer fires
193: ```
194: 
195: ### 7.1 Stunned / unavailable
196: 
197: If `stunned` or phase forbids free-run (End cinematic), emit neutral command (`axes 0`, buttons false).
198: 
199: ### 7.2 Average human position (flocking)
200: 
201: Design:
202: 
203: > Attempt to stand between all Human players. Average the position of all players. Tolerate a difference of up to **25% of the distance between the two furthest characters**.
204: 
205: **Algorithm (MVP):**
206: 
207: 1. Let `H` = haulers with `control == human` and not eliminated.
208: 2. If `|H| == 0` (AI-only room): use average of **all AI haulers** excluding self, or stand still / walk toward exit (config). Prefer exit bias so AI-only rooms still progress.
209: 3. If `|H| >= 1`:
210:    - `target.x = mean(h.x for h in H)`  
211:    - `target.y = mean(h.y for h in H)` (secondary; primarily horizontal game)
212: 4. Let `span = max pairwise distance among H` (if `|H| < 2`, use a fixed comfort radius, e.g. `4 * blockSize`).
213: 5. `tolerance = 0.25 * span` (or `0.25 * comfort` when single human).
214: 6. If `|self.x - target.x| <= tolerance` → `axes.x = 0` (stay put horizontally).
215: 7. Else `axes.x = sign(target.x - self.x)`.
216: 8. Vertical: only jump if target is significantly above and grounded and a crude “wall/ledge” heuristic says jump; otherwise `jump = false`. Duck only when pickup intent needs it.
217: 
218: **Tolerance band note:** “Between all humans” is approximated by mean + dead-zone; AI should not thrash when already in the pack.
219: 
220: ### 7.3 Treasure greed + load cap
221: 
222: Design:
223: 
224: > Pick up any treasure near them. Will **not** carry more than the most carried by a Human Player. Will drop or toss a lesser treasure to pick up a more valuable one.
225: 
226: **Load cap:**
227: 
228: ```text
229: maxHumanLoad = max(carryCount of human-controlled seats)
230:                // if no humans: use config default (e.g. 3) or uncapped low value
231: canPickup = self.carryCount < maxHumanLoad
232:             OR (upgrade intent will free a slot this tick sequence)
233: ```
234: 
235: **Proximity:**
236: 
237: - `pickupRadius` = ~1.5 blocks (tunable); must match sim duck/pickup reach.
238: - Prefer highest `valueGp` among free treasures in radius.
239: - Set `axes.y = +1` (down) when adjacent and `canPickup` to trigger duck/pickup.
240: - Do not trip/push (`action` alone) while intending pickup.
241: 
242: **Upgrade path:**
243: 
244: 1. If free treasure `T` in radius with `valueGp > min(self.carry values)` AND at cap:
245: 2. Issue drop chord: `action=true, axes.y=+1` (down) for one tick edge (server edge-detect).
246: 3. Subsequent ticks: move onto `T` and pickup.
247: 4. Prefer **drop** over **throw** for upgrades (throw is griefy / imprecise). Throw only if drop is blocked (stretch).
248: 
249: **Coin sacks:** Still subject to value comparison; prefer unique/set when values equal (rarity rank Unique/Set > Rare > Common).
250: 
251: ### 7.4 Switches
252: 
253: Design: *AI players will attempt to press any switch or button.*
254: 
255: MVP:
256: 
257: 1. Consider switches with `pressed == false` within `switchSeekRadius` (e.g. 8–12 blocks) or any switch that blocks progress if level metadata marks it required.
258: 2. Pick nearest by Manhattan/Euclidean distance.
259: 3. Move toward it (overrides flock if priority 1 active and switch is “actionable”).
260: 4. When overlapping switch volume: stand still; for heavy switches, only attempt if `weight` (self or nearby cooperative mass) meets requirement — if AI alone is too light, abandon and return to flock (don’t infinite-retry thrash).
261: 5. Avoid repeatedly toggling: once `pressed == true`, drop switch intent until unpressed again if design allows toggle-off.
262: 
263: ### 7.5 Stuck recovery (lightweight)
264: 
265: If `|vx| ~ 0` and `axes.x != 0` for `stuckTicks` (e.g. 45 ticks / 1.5s):
266: 
267: - Try jump once.
268: - If still stuck, reverse `axes.x` briefly or clear intent and replan next tick.
269: - No full pathfinder.
270: 
271: ### 7.6 Fork phase
272: 
273: Not free-run. Produce:
274: 
275: | Intent | Command |
276: |---|---|
277: | Path select | Bias `axes.y` toward option already leading, else random stable per seat (hash seatId + levelPath) |
278: | Argue | Pulse `jump` or `action` at a mild rate (~3–6 Hz random) so human mash still wins easily |
279: 
280: Stretch: follow majority human selection.
281: 
282: ### 7.7 End phase
283: 
284: AI does not enter name entry. Neutral inputs only. Ineligible for high scores.
